Living Well / Essay

Start here: the questions behind Living Well

Essay · 3 min read · Published October 8, 2026

Revision, 2026-10-09: A shorter introduction for casual visitors, with clear starting points and the new free-resource collection.

On this page
  1. A place for curiosity
  2. The interests that connect
  3. You do not have to improve anything today
  4. Three places to begin
  5. A personal site without invented personal stories
  6. One question to take with you

I’m interested in spirituality, life improvement, and technology that makes ordinary life better. Living Well is a place to explore how those interests meet.

A place for curiosity

This is a part of my personal website, not a course you need to complete. It brings together questions about meaning, attention, relationships, and what our tools are actually for. You can come with a spiritual tradition, a secular outlook, or a question you do not yet know how to phrase.

Some writing explores an idea. Some pages point to useful material elsewhere. Others help make a small part of an ordinary day less complicated. You do not have to approach all of those things in the same way.

The interests that connect

Building something useful raises the question of whom it serves. Making creative work raises questions about attention and expression. Decisions made under uncertainty raise questions about judgment and outcomes. Spirituality opens questions about meaning, wonder, and connection that need not become productivity techniques.

These are connections to explore, not a single system that explains everything. The Technology section focuses on tools. Poker and Creative Work remain separate interests. Living Well asks how ideas and tools fit into the life around them.

You do not have to improve anything today

A conversation, a poem, or a question can be worthwhile without becoming an assignment. A free afternoon does not need to produce an insight. There is room here for useful changes, but also for simply finding something interesting.

When a guide is helpful, use the smallest version that fits. A paper note or direct conversation may be better than an AI workflow. No resource on this website requires an AI subscription or asks you to upload your private reflections.

Three places to begin

For an idea, start with spiritual curiosity without pretending to be certain. For something outside the site, browse 18 selected free resources. For a practical example, open the fictional weekly reset, with and without AI.

Choose one that interests you. The topics and reading paths are there when you would like to explore further, not as a prerequisite for understanding the section.

A personal site without invented personal stories

The launch writing was prepared with AI assistance. It explores these interests without claiming experiences, experiments, or interviews that have not happened. Resources are selected for relevance; they are not automatically a list of things I have personally used or endorsed.

The editorial standards explain how factual sources, interpretation, and personal experience are kept distinct. Firsthand field notes will need actual observations. In the meantime, the questions and free material are here to browse at your own pace.

One question to take with you
